questions.q: In acute diseases (§§262 and 263), the patient's craving for particular food and drink should generally be:
opts: gratified within reason, as it comes from the instinct of the vital force
strictly refused, as it may antidote the remedy
replaced by a fixed hospital diet
satisfied only after the fever subsides
questions.why: §262–263: in acute disease the desires of the patient, guided by the vital force, should not be opposed, though a slight gratification of palliative wishes is enough.

questions.q: Prolapse of the rectum before or with the stool, with profuse gushing diarrhoea, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Podophyllum: prolapsus ani before or with stool (Boericke, Allen).

questions.q: Profuse, painless, gushing diarrhoea that is worse in the early morning suggests:
questions.why: Podophyllum: profuse, painless, gushing, offensive stools, worse early morning. Veratrum album has diarrhoea with collapse and cold sweat.

questions.q: Hypertension with hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis and suppressed plasma renin, without Cushingoid features, most suggests:
questions.why: Autonomous aldosterone excess causes sodium retention, potassium loss and alkalosis, with renin suppressed; renal artery stenosis raises renin.

opts: the venom of the honey bee
the contents of a scabies vesicle
the sputum of a tuberculous patient
questions.why: Pyrogenium (artificial sepsin) is made from lean beef allowed to decompose in water.

questions.q: In the liver, bilirubin is made water-soluble by conjugation with:
questions.why: UDP-glucuronyl transferase conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid; albumin only carries unconjugated bilirubin in plasma.

questions.q: Multiple, recurrent peptic ulcers including in the jejunum, with diarrhoea and very high gastric acid output, suggest a:
questions.why: Gastrin from a pancreatic or duodenal gastrinoma drives massive acid secretion, causing refractory ulcers at unusual sites and diarrhoea.

questions.q: The commonest site of a varicose ulcer is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. From venous hypertension.

questions.q: Impaired glucose tolerance is defined by a 2-hour plasma glucose, after a 75 g oral glucose load, of:
questions.why: A 2-hour value of 140 to 199 mg/dL is IGT, 200 or more is diabetes; 100 to 125 mg/dL fasting defines impaired fasting glucose.

questions.q: A very high blood pressure is termed a hypertensive emergency, rather than urgency, when there is:
opts: A diastolic BP above 120 mmHg without symptoms
Failure to respond to three antihypertensive drugs
questions.why: A hypertensive emergency is severe BP elevation with acute organ damage (encephalopathy, LVF, dissection, AKI); without it the situation is urgency.
